steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Clave is a two-bar rhythmic pattern (3-2 or 2-3) that underpins virtually all Latin music — all other rhythmic parts align with the clave.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Bossa nova is a Brazilian style blending samba rhythms with jazz harmonies — gentle, syncopated guitar patterns and soft vocal delivery.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Salsa features piano montuno (repeated syncopated pattern), brass riffs, and layered percussion — it creates high-energy dance music through rhythmic complexity.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Tango and habanera share the distinctive rhythmic pattern (dotted quaver-semiquaver-quaver-quaver) — tango added dramatic expression and bandoneón.

steps.title: Try it yourself

Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use contemporary latin music in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A detailed description using precise musical vocabulary (e.g. specific terms from the AQA elements list), referencing a named piece with accurate observations about how the elements are used and their | A comparison of two pieces identifying similarities and differences in how contemporary latin music are used, explaining the different effects created in each musical context, using comparative langua | A practical application showing understanding of how contemporary latin music can be manipulated in composition or performance, with specific examples of choices made and their intended effect.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use PRECISE musical vocabulary — not vague descriptions like it sounds nice Reference SPECIFIC musical elements when analysing any piece For listening questions: identify elements FIRST, then explain their effect For study pieces: know the context, structure and key features in detail For performing: focus on accuracy, expression and interpretation For composing: show development of ideas, not just repetition
